business_problem: Figma wanted teams to turn ideas and static designs into interactive software much faster, reduce the friction between design and development, and let non-coders prototype without rebuilding designs by hand.
solution_summary: Figma integrated Claude into two creation paths: Figma Sites, where designers describe interaction changes against an existing web design, and Figma Make, where users start from a prompt or an existing Figma design and receive a working prototype or app. Claude generates the underlying code while preserving design intent, animations, responsive behavior, and pixel-level details instead of asking teams to recreate layouts from scratch. Figma continuously evaluates new Claude models and exposes the latest releases through an experimental-models setting, using Claude Sonnet as the model that first made the product viable and Claude Opus 4.6 for more complex, interactive builds. The round-trip between Figma Design and Make lets teams copy designs in, generate code-backed software, then return the result to the canvas for side-by-side iteration.
